questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The work done by a variable force acting along a straight line is given by:
options: The area under the force-displacement graph
The slope of the force-displacement graph
questions.explanation: W = ∫F dx, which is exactly the area under the curve. Simply multiplying force by displacement works only when the force is constant.
questions.ncertReference: Physics Class 11, Chapter 5: Work, Energy and Power

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two springs of force constants k₁ and k₂ are connected in parallel and support a mass. The effective force constant of the combination is:
questions.explanation: In parallel both springs stretch by the same amount and share the load, so the constants add. In series they add as reciprocals, like resistors the other way round.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The relation between the critical angle C and the refractive index μ of a denser medium with respect to air is:
questions.explanation: Applying Snell's law at the critical angle, where the refracted ray grazes the surface at 90°, gives sin C = 1/μ. A denser medium therefore has a smaller critical angle.
questions.ncertReference: Physics Class 12, Chapter 9: Ray Optics and Optical Instruments

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The volume of 0.5 M HCl needed to prepare 500 mL of 0.1 M HCl by dilution is:
questions.explanation: On dilution the moles of solute do not change, so M₁V₁ = M₂V₂ gives 0.5 × V = 0.1 × 500, that is V = 100 mL, made up to 500 mL with water.
questions.ncertReference: Chemistry Class 11, Chapter 1: Some Basic Concepts of Chemistry

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The bond order of the superoxide ion O₂⁻ according to molecular orbital theory is:
questions.explanation: O₂⁻ has 10 bonding and 7 antibonding electrons, so the bond order is (10 - 7)/2 = 1.5. Adding electrons to an antibonding orbital weakens and lengthens the bond.
questions.ncertReference: Chemistry Class 11, Chapter 4: Chemical Bonding and Molecular Structure

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Heating sodium phenoxide with carbon dioxide under pressure followed by acidification gives salicylic acid. This reaction is known as:
questions.explanation: Salicylic acid is the starting material for aspirin. The Reimer-Tiemann reaction uses chloroform and alkali instead, and gives salicylaldehyde.
questions.ncertReference: Chemistry Class 12, Chapter 7: Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: Ginger and turmeric are examples of which underground stem modification?
questions.explanation: A rhizome grows horizontally and bears nodes, internodes and scaly leaves, which proves it is a stem and not a root. Potato is a tuber and Colocasia a corm.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 11, Chapter 5: Morphology of Flowering Plants

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: Although several pigments absorb light, the molecule that actually acts as the reaction centre in both photosystems is:
questions.explanation: The accessory pigments only harvest light and hand the energy on to chlorophyll a, which alone releases the electron. They also protect chlorophyll a from photo-oxidation.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 11, Chapter 11: Photosynthesis in Higher Plants

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: Haemodialysis, used to treat kidney failure, works on the principle of:
options: Active transport of urea into the dialysing fluid
Diffusion of wastes across a semipermeable membrane down a concentration gradient
questions.explanation: The dialysing fluid has the same composition as plasma but no nitrogenous wastes, so urea diffuses out while useful solutes stay. Heparin is added to stop the blood clotting.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 11, Chapter 16: Excretory Products and their Elimination

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: A rasping, file-like feeding organ called the radula is characteristic of phylum:
questions.explanation: Molluscs such as snails use the radula to scrape food. Their body is soft and unsegmented, usually covered by a calcareous shell, and the visceral mass is covered by a mantle.
